rapport_notes: Warm, responsive, congratulatory tone; good active listening; maintained friendly cadence throughout.
process_discipline_notes: Repeated 'confirm inventory is complete' multiple times without waiting for silence after open questions; no silence held after estimate presentation before pivoting to availability.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Missing the full framing. Rep says 'before we get too much in the weed, I wanna make sure that I'm answering the questions that are important to you' but does not frame the ask with a time-box or promise of an accurate quote in return.
evidence_quotes.agenda: Rep asked: 'do you have any of those kind of top of mind right now that I can kind of dive into?' — Asked before probing starts. Customer replied that they are repeat customers and don't have concerns.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer said 'I know I'm pretty good' (indicating no concerns) and had previously used Einstein twice. Rep acknowledged but did not probe deeper or ask 'what else is on your mind' — no real two-layer follow-up occurred because there were no concerns raised to dig into. Per rubric N/A logic, this scores full credit (15 pts N/A).
evidence_quotes.communication_covered: Rep: 'you'll also see that trip fee is already included in that estimate' and 'I'm gonna send you a confirmation email, of course... I do have all the notes in here. I have your complete inventory list in here for the movers to see' — covers email/communication but does not name crew lead or day-before call specifics.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep: 'normally, typically a move when we're moving like a 1400 square foot house, it takes about six to eight hours, since we're only moving these few items that we have listed here, I'm gonna get us set about four and a half to five and a half' — gives range and personalizes to the reduced inventory.
evidence_quotes.estimate_window: Rep: 'again if everything is already wrapped up and ready to go, then I mean, I would think that it would be even less than that timeframe' and 'you only pay for the time you use anyway, so while we're giving you this estimate, if it gets closer to I don't know, three to four hours then that's all you end up paying for anyway' — acknowledges variability.
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: Rep: 'if it gets closer to I don't know, three to four hours then that's all you end up paying for anyway' — covers the concept of paying less if crew beats estimate.
evidence_quotes.close_missing: No rate-lock line; no explicit 'would you like our help with your move' ask. Call ends with 'I'm gonna send you a confirmation email' but no booking confirmation or explicit close.

top_strength: Excellent discovery of reduced inventory — rep listened to the customer, adjusted the estimate downward significantly (from 6–8 hours to 4.5–5.5 hours), and factored in the drive time, demonstrating logistics accuracy and responsiveness to actual needs.
coaching_note: Close the call with an explicit rate-lock statement and a clear booking confirmation ask; you have repeat-customer goodwill — seal it with 'Your rate locks when you book — shall I get you confirmed for September 22nd?' rather than trailing off at confirmation-email delivery.
